skill.summary: Create AI images and image edits from CLI-ready inference.sh model examples.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed the pipe-to-shell installer on SKILL.md line 22 as a critical risk. The related network URL on line 22 is also risky because it downloads executable installer content. The remaining backtick and URL findings are Markdown documentation, model identifiers, or placeholder examples with no prompt injection or covert exfiltration evidence.

remediation.issue: Pipe-to-shell installer in the quick-start instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the installer with a package-manager command or a download flow that verifies checksum or signature before execution.

remediation.issue: Executable installation examples appear inside a skill focused on running inference.sh apps.
remediation.suggestion: Keep executable examples aligned with allowed tools and move optional installation of other skills to non-executable documentation.

remediation.issue: Remote image generation sends prompts and image URLs to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note warning users not to submit confidential prompts, private images, or customer data.

content.value_statement: Creating visual assets across many image models is slow when each provider has different steps. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical inference.sh CLI examples for generation, editing, upscaling, and stitching.
actual_capabilities: Shows inference.sh commands for text-to-image generation with FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, and Reve models.
Lists image model identifiers and their intended strengths for faster model selection.
Provides examples for product photos, landscapes, posters with text, portraits, and cyberpunk scenes.
Includes image upscaling and multi-image stitching examples through inference.sh apps.
Supports CLI workflows in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when inference.sh access is available.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, an account login, and network access to remote model providers.
Model availability, pricing, latency, and output quality are controlled outside the skill.
Prompts and image URLs may be sent to external services during generation or editing.
Does not provide local image safety checks, rights review, or asset storage management.

use_cases.title: Create Concept Art
use_cases.description: Generate visual directions for characters, scenes, posters, and product ideas using model-specific examples.

use_cases.title: Produce Marketing Visuals
use_cases.description: Draft social graphics, campaign images, and product mockups with repeatable prompt structures.

use_cases.title: Prototype Image Workflows
use_cases.description: Test inference.sh image apps from a terminal before adding them to scripts or product experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an image of a calm mountain lake at sunrise. Recommend one inference.sh model and explain the expected style.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model for a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a product mockup with clean studio lighting and readable label text. Compare two suitable models and recommend one.

prompt_templates.title: Upscale or Edit an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an existing approved image URL to plan an upscale or edit. Include privacy cautions and the model choice.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repeatable Asset Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a repeatable workflow for generating five branded social images with consistent style, aspect ratios, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Create a studio product photo of a ceramic mug for an online store.
output_examples.output: A recommended image model, a refined product prompt, suggested aspect ratio, and notes about lighting and background consistency.

output_examples.input: Make a poster that includes clear headline text.
output_examples.output: A text-rendering model recommendation, prompt wording for the poster, and guidance to review spelling in the generated image.

output_examples.input: Upscale an approved image URL for a presentation slide.
output_examples.output: A privacy reminder, an upscaler recommendation, and expected output checks for sharpness, artifacts, and final resolution.

best_practices: Define subject, style, aspect ratio, lighting, and text needs before choosing a model.
Use only approved image URLs and avoid sending confidential assets to remote services.
Verify installation sources and account permissions before running inference.sh commands.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private customer images, unreleased designs, or secrets into image prompts or URLs.
Do not run remote installer scripts without source verification and checksum or signature checks.
Do not launch many high-cost generations without confirming budget, resolution, and review limits.

faq.question: What does this skill help generate?
faq.answer: It helps generate AI images, product mockups, concept art, posters, upscaled images, and stitched image layouts through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it work without an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: No. The examples require the inference.sh CLI, account login, and network access to run remote image models.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for image upscaling, text rendering, and workflows that use existing image URLs.

faq.question: Are generated prompts or images kept local?
faq.answer: No. The workflow uses remote inference.sh apps, so prompts and image URLs may leave the local environment.

faq.question: Is the installer command safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The audit flags the pipe-to-shell installer pattern and recommends a verified installation method instead.
